answer: Each identity buys one willow bark lot from the orchard registry, locks 80 credits as bond and posts lot code and weight. An auditor titrates the sample against a kernel reference and recomputes tannin from weight and titre; an assay outside the band, or a reused lot code, burns the bond. The k-th lot costs 38+9(k-1) credits, so 1,000 fakes pay 4,533,500 in fees plus 80,000 bonds at risk; lots are single-use. A rented-bark ring fails: one lot yields one assay record under one key, and a resubmitted code flags both claims. An honest agent pays 38 once, bond back after a clean assay.
